📥 媒体下载（封面 / 视频 / 图文图片）

默认关闭。开启后会在爬取的同时把媒体文件下载到本地，按帖子聚合存放：

<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="# 命令行开关

uv run main.py --platform xhs --type detail --specified_id <帖子URL或ID> --get_media true

uv run main.py --platform xhs --type detail --specified_id < 帖子URL或ID > --get_media true

# 或在 config/base_config.py 中设置 ENABLE_GET_MEDIA = True

落盘结构 （ SAVE_DATA_PATH 为空时落在 data/ 下）：

<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="data/xhs/media/{帖子ID}/

├── cover.jpg # 封面

├── video.mp4 # 视频（B站为 DASH 合流产物）

├── cover.jpg # 封面

├── video.mp4 # 视频（B站为 DASH 合流产物）

├── 001.jpg # 图文帖的图片

└── 001_live.mp4 # 对应图片的实况随附视频（有实况时）

支持平台 ：小红书、抖音、快手、B站、微博。贴吧与知乎的数据结构中没有媒体字段，暂不支持。

实况照片（Live Photo） ：抖音和小红书统一由 config/base_config.py 中的 DOWNLOAD_LIVE_PHOTO 控制，默认 True ，仅在 ENABLE_GET_MEDIA 开启时生效。设为 False 后只保存静态图，普通视频下载不受影响。实况视频与静态图使用相同的原始图片序号（如 001.jpg / 001_live.mp4 ），缺失媒体时保留序号空位。这里保存的是独立图片与随附视频，不合成手机相册的 Live Photo，也不转换为 GIF。小红书 Web 返回的实况视频可能自带水印，下载会保留该视频的原始内容。

安装 ffmpeg 后可走 DASH 路径获取最高画质（音视频分轨下载后无损合流）；未安装时自动降级为 mp4 直链，产物名为 video-durl.mp4 以便区分

清晰度由 config/bilibili_config.py 的 BILI_QN 控制（默认 80 = 1080p）；未登录或权限不足时若高清取流被拒，会自动逐档降级到实际可下载的清晰度

媒体下载失败只记录日志，不会中断爬取

已存在的文件会被跳过；需要重新下载时删掉对应目录即可

🖥️ WebUI 可视化操作界面

MediaCrawler 提供了基于 Web 的可视化操作界面，无需命令行也能轻松使用爬虫功能。

开发时需要同时启动后端 API 服务和前端 Vite 开发服务器：

<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="# 终端 1：启动 API 服务器（默认端口 8080）

uv run uvicorn api.main:app --port 8080 --reload

# 终端 2：启动前端开发服务器

npm run dev # 默认在 5173 端口启动，并代理 /api 到 8080"> # 终端 1：启动 API 服务器（默认端口 8080）

uv run uvicorn api.main:app --port 8080 --reload

# 终端 2：启动前端开发服务器

npm run dev # 默认在 5173 端口启动，并代理 /api 到 8080

启动成功后，访问 http://localhost:5173/ 即可打开 WebUI 界面。

首次打开会进行环境检测（调用 /api/env/check ），请确保后端服务已启动。如果检测失败，可点击「跳过检测」临时跳过。

Paperclip is the app people use to manage AI agents for work.

Open-source orchestration for teams of AI agents.

If OpenClaw is an employee , Paperclip is the company .

Paperclip is a Node.js server and React UI that orchestrates a team of AI agents to run a business. Bring your own agents, assign goals, and track work and costs from one dashboard. Choose models and harnesses per agent while keeping your team's tasks, skills, permissions, and history in one place.

It looks like a task manager. Under the hood: org charts, budgets, governance, goal alignment, and agent coordination.

Manage business goals, not pull requests.

Define the goal

"Build the #1 AI note-taking app to $1M MRR."

Hire the team

CEO, CTO, engineers, designers, marketers — any bot, any provider.

Review strategy. Set budgets. Hit go. Monitor from the dashboard.

If it can receive a heartbeat, it's hired.

Custom processes, HTTP endpoints, and external adapter packages extend the roster. See the adapter overview for setup and capabilities.

Paperclip is right for you if

✅ You want to build autonomous AI organizations

✅ You coordinate many different agents (OpenClaw, Codex, Claude, Cursor) toward a common goal

✅ You have 20 simultaneous Claude Code terminals open and lose track of what everyone is doing

✅ You want agents running autonomously 24/7 , but still want to audit work and chime in when needed

✅ You want to monitor costs and enforce budgets

✅ You want a process for managing agents that feels like using a task manager

✅ You want to manage your autonomous businesses from your phone

The four pillars

Four things have to work for an organization of AI agents to actually produce: the tasks, the org, the training, and the infrastructure. Paperclip is built around exactly those four pillars.

What it covers

Agentic Task Manager — Declare intent. Agents work. You verify the output.

Everyone, daily

Tasks, approvals & review gates · proactive agent coworkers · auditable routines & workflows · verify from diffs, screenshots & tests

Org Chart for Agents — Roles, permissions & boundaries for humans and agents.

Mixed human + agent org chart · responsibilities, delegation, specialization · governance: who can do what · scoped secrets & company boundaries · connection permissions & responsible-user identities

Agent Employee Training — Design, train & evaluate your AI employees.

Skill Studio & shared org-wide skills · evals & saved test runs · active learning loops & quality metrics · performance reviews for agents · saved test inputs · skill version history & restore · reusable team templates

<a id="user-content-prime-agent-a-self-improving-rlm-harness" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink:

Prime Agent: A Self-Improving RLM Harness

" href="#prime-agent-a-self-improving-rlm-harness">

Documentation •

Prime Agent is an open-source coding and research agent for general and long-running work. It is designed around two core abstractions:

The Recursive Language Model (RLM) treats context as variables ( prompt-as-a-variable ) and tools like recursive subagents as function calls ( programmatic tool /sub-agent calling ) inside a persistent REPL.

The Continual Harness stores supplemental prompts, memories, skill descriptions, and reusable subagent specifications as durable state that Prime Agent can refine through small, evidence-backed updates, local to the session by default.

Install the latest stable version with the one-command installer:

curl -fsSL https://app.primeintellect.ai/prime-agent/install.sh | sh

On Windows, install from PowerShell:

irm https: // app.primeintellect.ai / prime - agent / install.ps1 | iex

The Windows installer downloads the latest stable Windows x64 build and verifies its checksum before installation.

Why Prime Agent

Prime Agent combines a persistent Python control environment with durable harness state, so useful working context and reusable operating patterns can outlive a single chat window.

Everything is programmatic: a persistent Python REPL is the built-in model tool; file operations, shell commands, tool use, subagents, and context management happen through code.

Subagents are built in: rlm.spawn(...) spawns real child agents for parallel or background work and returns their results programmatically.

The harness can improve: /refine reviews the current trajectory and can apply small, evidence-backed updates to supplemental harness state. It never rewrites the immutable base system prompt, and recorded snapshots support rollback.

Skills can be executable: Python skills in your user configuration are imported into the kernel; repository skills provide Markdown instructions without automatic code execution.

Sessions run in the background: daemon-backed agents keep running when the terminal disconnects and can be reattached later.

Agents communicate directly: running agents can exchange messages and orchestrate one another without routing everything through the user.

Long tasks keep moving: automatic compaction, persistent goals, heartbeats, schedules, autonomous mode, and retained subagents preserve progress across turns and terminal sessions.

Connect Slack from /mcp or run /mcp login slack inside Prime Agent to search

your workspace and use Slack tools. See the Slack connector guide

for OAuth setup and troubleshooting.

Google Drive and Google Sheets

Connect Google's official Drive and Sheets MCP servers with your own Google

OAuth client: add them to mcpServers with clientId , clientSecret ,

callbackPort , and scopes , then run /mcp login <name> . See the

Google Drive and Google Sheets guide for the

Google Cloud setup and the tool mapping.

Clipboard over SSH and tmux

Prime Agent uses the local clipboard tool (such as pbcopy ) when available. In tmux it asks the attached tmux client to forward a clipboard buffer if that client advertises the Ms capability. This works with tmux's default set-clipboard external , unlike application-origin OSC 52. Without tmux, remote copies request delivery using OSC 52. Terminal requests cannot confirm that your local clipboard changed, so Prime Agent reports them as unconfirmed.

Nested tmux servers and terminals may still block delivery. An outer tmux with set-clipboard external can reject the inner server's OSC 52. In that case, run tmux set -s set-clipboard on on the outer server, or use native terminal selection (Shift-drag in most terminals; Option-drag in iTerm2) followed by Cmd-C. macOS Terminal.app does not support OSC 52; iTerm2 requires its “Applications in terminal may access clipboard” setting.

Custom certificate authorities

HTTPS requests trust your operating system's trust store together with the bundled Mozilla roots. For servers behind a custom CA, point NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS at a PEM bundle of your CA certificates — the same variable the Node/TypeScript build honors:

export NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/path/to/your-ca.pem

Each transport reads the variable once when its first client is initialized. The background daemon keeps the environment it started with, so run prime-agent shutdown after changing it.

Getting Started

Start Prime Agent from the repository or directory you want it to work in:

<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="cd /path/to/project

prime-agent"> cd /path/to/project

On first launch, run /login to choose a subscription or API-key provider. Prime Agent works in the current directory and can run commands and modify files there. Use a disposable clone, clean worktree, or another checkpoint you can inspect and restore.

π RuView is a WiFi sensing platform that turns radio signals into spatial intelligence.

Every WiFi router already fills your space with radio waves. When people move, breathe, or even sit still, they disturb those waves in measurable ways. RuView captures these disturbances using Channel State Information (CSI) from low-cost ESP32 sensors and turns them into actionable data: who's there, what they're doing, and whether they're okay.

What it senses:

Presence and occupancy — detect people through walls, count them, track entries and exits

Vital signs — breathing rate and heart rate, contactless, while sleeping or sitting

Activity recognition — walking, sitting, gestures, falls — from temporal CSI patterns

Environment mapping — RF fingerprinting identifies rooms, detects moved furniture, spots new objects

Camera-free pose — estimate 17 body keypoints from WiFi CSI

Built-in model workflow — record CSI, train models, load RVF files, and switch LoRA profiles

The AI-Powered Life Operating System

LifeOS-8.761.0-release.mp4

LifeOS is a General Purpose AI Harness for doing anything you want to do in life and work with AI. It captures who you are, what you care about, and where you're trying to go, then uses AI that knows you to help you get there.

And because it has your full context, it makes everything you do more efficient and effective, from building apps, to starting a business, to creative projects… basically anything .

The whole system works on one central concept: moving from your Current State to your Ideal State — in pursuit of Euphoric Surprise.

⭐ If LifeOS is useful to you, star the repo

Stars help more people find the project and keep it moving. It takes one click.

⚠️ Your Security Is Your Responsibility

LifeOS is fundamentally one person's personal AI harness, published as-is, and it is constantly in flux: security features are added, enhanced, removed, modified and adjusted from release to release. The security of any LifeOS component, and of the system as a whole, is not guaranteed. Responsibility for the security of your system is yours, not the LifeOS authors' or contributors'.

Before anything is installed, the installer asks: "Do you understand that you are responsible for the security of your own system and that we are not responsible?" It goes ahead only if you answer yes. See SECURITY.md .

Give it to your AI. LifeOS is installed by an AI, so the install is just a prompt. Paste this into your AI coding harness — Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Hermes, or any capable agent — and it does the whole setup for you:

Read https://ourlifeos.ai/install and install LifeOS for me.

Your AI reads the install page and walks the setup, asking permission before it touches anything.

Prefer the terminal? There's a one-line shortcut for Claude Code on macOS/Linux:

curl -fsSL https://ourlifeos.ai/install.sh | bash

Either path needs a capable AI coding harness — we build and run on Claude Code — and bun .

Core Components

The unique features — the parts you won't find anywhere else. Anything a good harness already provides on its own (built-in subagents, for example) isn't listed; this is only what LifeOS adds. See them live and click through on ourlifeos.ai .

LifeOS ships 97 public skills, from research, security, writing and art to video, publishing and your home. Browse them all on the site.

Browse all skills →

How is LifeOS different from using an AI harness on its own?

Your harness gives you raw capability. LifeOS is the layer on top that makes it yours — a system that knows your goals, people, and context, and keeps working toward them:

Persistent memory — Your DA remembers past sessions, decisions, and learnings

Custom skills — Specialized capabilities for the things you do most

Your context — Goals, contacts, preferences—all available without re-explaining

Intelligent routing — Say "research this" and the right workflow triggers automatically

Self-improvement — The system modifies itself based on what it learns

Your harness is the engine. LifeOS is everything else that makes it your car.

What harness does LifeOS run on?

Any high-end one. LifeOS is harness-agnostic by design — it's built on universal primitives (hooks, skills, context files, agentic routing), not one vendor's features. The code is TypeScript and Bash, and the core ideas — TELOS, the Algorithm, skills, memory — port to any capable agent.

Daniel builds and runs it on Claude Code , so that's the most-tested path today. But LifeOS isn't locked to it, and it's designed to run wherever your AI does.

How is this different from fabric?

Fabric is a collection of AI prompts (patterns) for specific tasks. It's focused on what to ask AI .

LifeOS is infrastructure for how your DA operates —memory, skills, routing, context, self-improvement. They're complementary. Many LifeOS users integrate Fabric patterns into their skills.

Back up first — Before any upgrade: cp -r ~/.claude ~/.claude-backup-$(date +%Y%m%d)

USER/ is safe — Your customizations in USER/ are never touched by the installer or upgrades

Settings merge, not overwrite — The installer only updates identity and version fields; your hooks, statusline, and custom config are preserved

Git-backed — Version control everything, roll back when needed

History is preserved — Your DA's memory survives mistakes

DA can fix it — Your DA helped build it, it can help repair it

Re-install — Run the installer again; it detects existing installations and merges intelligently

WeatherNext 2

This repo contains the code for WeatherNext 2 (WN2), the global, medium-range

atmospheric and cyclone forecasting model developed by Google DeepMind and

Google Research.

It also contains code for prior generation models

Accessing Forecast Data Feeds

If you are interested in directly accessing daily data feeds of WN2 model

outputs rather than running the model yourself, we provide them across multiple

Google Cloud

(including Earth Engine, BigQuery, and Vertex AI).

WeatherLab (including cyclone tracks).

OpenMeteo (including an API and interactive builder).

Model Guide & Documentation: Google Developers WeatherNext Guide

WeatherNext Cyclones Paper: Operational tropical cyclone forecasting

FGN/WN2 Technical Report: Skillful joint probabilistic weather

forecasting from marginals

(arXiv:2506.10772)

WeatherNext 2 Blog Post: WeatherNext 2: Our most advanced weather forecasting model

WeatherNext Cyclones Blog Post: WeatherNext: AI model achieves breakthrough in forecasting cyclones

Older Models

This repository serves as the primary home for the WeatherNext family models.

Alongside WN2, this repository also hosts the code and documentation for our

legacy and specialized models:

WeatherNext Graph : Deterministic

medium-range weather forecasting using graph neural networks. Published as

WeatherNext Gen : Diffusion-based ensemble

forecasting for medium-range weather. Published as GenCast.

Provided Pretrained Models

This repository provides code to run the different versions of WeatherNext 2 and

WeatherNext Cyclones. The only difference between them is that WN2 can also

predict 100m wind. In particular, WN2 also forecasts cyclones with the exact

same algorithm as WN Cyclones. Their weights are different due to independent

training runs.

WeatherNext 2

WeatherNext2_<2025 (Used Operationally): 0.25° resolution (~30km).

Fine-tuned on ECMWF HRES data and designed to be initialized directly from

operational HRES initial conditions rather than ERA5 reanalysis. Trained on

data through 2024. Corresponding weights files:

WeatherNext2_<2025_model{1,2,3,4}.npz .

WeatherNext Cyclones - models which reproduce the results in paper

WeatherNextCyclones_<2025 (Used Operationally): 0.25° resolution. The

model that ran live during the 2025 Atlantic hurricane season, publicly

referred to as FNV3 (NHC's postprocessed version was called GDMI). Trained

on data through 2024. The paper appendix contains a partial evaluation of

2025 in NHC basins for this model checkpoint, and how the tracker

improvement in September 2025 improved results. Corresponding weights files:

WeatherNextCyclones_<2025_model{1,2,3,4}.npz .

WeatherNextCyclones_<2024 : 0.25° resolution. Reproduces results from the

paper on 2024. Trained on data through 2023. Corresponding weights files:

WeatherNextCyclones_<2024_model{1,2,3,4}.npz .

WeatherNextCyclones_<2023 : 0.25° resolution. Reproduces results from the

paper on 2023. Trained on data through 2022. Corresponding weights files:

WeatherNextCyclones_<2023_model{1,2,3,4}.npz .

WeatherNext Cyclones Mini

WeatherNextCyclones_Mini_<2024 : 1° resolution. A lightweight version

suitable for lower memory and compute constraints (e.g., local testing or

single TPUs or GPUs). Not expected to match the performance of the larger

versions. Forecasts the same things as WeatherNext2_<2025, including

cyclones. Trained on data through 2023. Corresponding weights file:

WeatherNextCyclones_Mini_<2024.npz .

WeatherNextCyclones_Mini_<2023 : As above, but only trained on data through

2022. Corresponding weights file: WeatherNextCyclones_Mini_<2023.npz .

Evaluation results for WeatherNextCyclones_Mini can be found in the appendix

WeatherNext Cyclones Paper .

Quick Start Guide

The easiest way to get started with WeatherNext 2 is by running our interactive

Colab Notebook , which can be opened from

Colaboratory .

This notebook defaults to WeatherNext Cyclones Mini, which we recommend running

using the v5e-1 runtime, available for free as a Colab runtime. However, the

notebook can also be used to run the other models enumerated above (but these

will require a v5p accelerator).

In general, we recommend running WeatherNext 2 on TPU where possible, since its

implementation has been optimised for it. However, if choosing to run on GPU,

the attention implementation must be switched, as shown in the demo notebook.

The non-Mini models require H100 for sufficient VRAM. The Mini models should

manage inference on a P100.

Pre-trained weights and sample data are available on our Google Cloud

Inside the notebook, you will learn how to:

Automatically load the required model weights from our storage bucket.

Load initial state weather data (e.g., HRES initial conditions).

Initialize the WN2 (FGN) architecture.

Run auto-regressive rollout steps to generate a forecast prediction.

Visualize the outputs (e.g., temperature, wind speed, geopotential height).

Run the direct tracker on model outputs to obtain track data for cyclones.

Compute the training loss on model predictions and targets, and take a

gradient step.

Installation

This is research code provided as-is for the purpose of running and

experimenting with the published models. There are no guarantees of API

stability and future updates may introduce breaking changes without notice. We

recommend pinning to a specific release.

pip install git+https://github.com/google-deepmind/weathernext.git@v0.3.0

Model Weights

To run WeatherNext 2 or WeatherNext Cyclones, you will need to download the

pre-trained model weights. You can access the weights on Google Cloud

Code-Graph-RAG

Code-Graph-RAG parses a multi-language codebase with Tree-sitter, sharpened by compiler-grade frontends and runtime traces where available, builds a knowledge graph of its structure in an embedded graph database that needs no server, and lets you query, edit, and optimise that code in plain English. It works across a monorepo of mixed languages under one unified graph schema.

1. Index: cgr start --update-graph parses a repository into a knowledge graph (sped up)

2. Ask: cgr start answers questions and edits code, grounded in that graph

Latest News 🔥

Type Handling : Improved handling of type context managers, walrus operators, and match binding targets in both Python and TypeScript.

Rename Refinement : Prevented Go renames from unexporting names used by other packages.

Profile Naming : Corrected the naming of pprof profiles to avoid "malformed" errors when no samples are present.

Output Budget : Increased the Anthropic output budget to improve the default thinking experience.

Module Resolution : Resolved issues with module resolution in various scenarios, including ES module default imports and bare name bindings.

Dead Code Elimination : Removed dead code roots associated with IPython rich-display methods.

Incremental Refresh : Improved incremental refresh to ensure callers are updated when dispatch targets change.

See NEWS.md for the full history.

What It Does

Point Code-Graph-RAG at a repository and it reads every source file, extracts functions, classes, methods, modules, and the relationships between them, and stores the result as an interconnected graph. Once the graph exists you can:

Ask questions about the codebase in natural language and get answers grounded in the real structure.

Retrieve the actual source of any function, class, or method by name or by intent.

Edit code through the agent with AST-based surgical patching and a diff preview before anything changes.

Optimise code against language best practices or your own coding standards.

Find dead code by walking call and reference edges from entry points.

Search and rewrite structurally by AST pattern with ast-grep.

Overlay runtime behaviour: trace a test run (or pull production eBPF profiles) with cgr trace and merge the calls that actually happened into the graph, exposing dispatch that static analysis cannot see.

How It Works

The system has two components:

Multi-language parser. A Tree-sitter based parser reads the codebase and ingests functions, classes, methods, modules, and their relationships into the graph under a single language-agnostic schema. Where a toolchain is available, compiler-grade frontends layer exact facts on top (libclang for C/C++, go/types for Go, and opt-in Roslyn, javac and Jedi for C#, Java and Python), and dynamic tracing merges calls observed at runtime. Tree-sitter stays the backbone: a trace only sees code that ran, and a compiler frontend only covers what its toolchain can build.

RAG system ( codebase_rag/ ). An interactive CLI that turns natural language into Cypher queries, retrieves matching code, and drives AI-powered editing and optimisation.

<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="Source Code -> Tree-sitter Parser -> AST Analysis -> Knowledge Graph

User Query -> AI Model (Cypher Gen) -> Cypher Query -> Graph Results -> Response"> Source Code -> Tree-sitter Parser -> AST Analysis -> Knowledge Graph

User Query -> AI Model (Cypher Gen) -> Cypher Query -> Graph Results -> Response

The graph is stored in an embedded SQLite file by default. Memgraph and Neo4j are opt-in backends that run the same Cypher; Graph Backends compares them.

See the Architecture Overview and Graph Schema for the full picture.

Supported Languages

Python, TypeScript, TSX, JavaScript, Rust, Go, Java, C, C++, C#, PHP, Lua, Dart, and Julia are fully supported. Scala is in development, and Ruby, Kotlin, Swift, Elixir, Haskell, Solidity, Bash, and Nix have structural support (modules, functions, classes where the language has them, and imports) through the pluggable ast-grep tier. See the Language Support matrix for per-language capabilities.

Installation

cgr is published to PyPI. Install it system-wide with the treesitter-full (tree-sitter grammars), ast-grep (Ruby, Kotlin, Swift, Elixir, Haskell, Solidity, Bash, Nix) and semantic (vector search) extras:

uv tool install "code-graph-rag[treesitter-full,ast-grep,semantic]"

# or with pipx

pipx install "code-graph-rag[treesitter-full,ast-grep,semantic]""> # with uv (recommended)

The open-source control plane for coding agents.

T3 Code runs the coding agents on your machine and gives them one fast interface. Start a thread at your desk, then approve the next step from your phone.

It works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Grok Build, Antigravity, Kiro, Pi, Muse Code, fx, and any ACP agent. If an agent is set up on your computer, T3 Code can control it.

What you get

Your subscriptions. T3 Code does not resell tokens. It drives the agents you are already signed in to.

Every agent in one place. Change models in the middle of a thread. Let Claude hand a task to Codex.

Desktop, web, and phone. One server, and every client shows the same threads. There are apps for iOS and Android.

Remote ready. Run agents on any machine. Connect over your local network, Tailscale, or T3 Connect .

Git built in. Each thread can work in its own worktree. Review the diff, then commit, push, and open a pull request with one button.

Fast. Performance is a feature here. We measure it, and we treat a dropped frame as a bug.

Open. MIT licensed. If you don't like something, fork it.

Download T3 Code for macOS, Windows, or Linux. You can also use a package manager:

brew install --cask t3-code

winget install T3Tools.T3Code or scoop install extras/t3code

yay -S t3code-bin

nix profile add github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable#t3code

Debian, Ubuntu

.deb from Releases

Command line

This installs the t3 command. Run t3 to start the server and open the web app.

curl -fsSL https://t3.codes/install.sh | sh

On Windows, in PowerShell:

irm https: // t3.codes / install.ps1 | iex

To try it once without an install, run npx t3@latest .

Get the app from the App Store or Google Play . Then follow remote access to connect it to your computer.

Sign in to an agent

T3 Code needs one agent that is installed and signed in. For example, install Claude Code and run claude auth login , or install Codex CLI and run codex login .

Provider setup has the steps for each agent. Install T3 Code covers nightly builds, AppImage, WSL, and NixOS.

"Wait, what are you selling me?"

Nothing. We built T3 Code because we wanted the best possible development experience with agents. We were inspired by existing solutions like the Codex desktop app, Conductor, Claude Desktop and Cursor Glass, but none met our bar.

We wanted something performant, remote-ready, and truly open. If we ever go the wrong direction, we want you to have everything you need to fork and build the tool that you want.

NASA Seeks Next Generation of Explorers to Join Astronaut Corps

Jessica Taveau

Nov 07, 2026

RELEASE 26-093

NASA Headquarters

Johnson Space Center

NASA announced its 2025 Astronaut Candidate Class on Sept. 22, 2025, at the agency’s Johnson Space Center in Houston.

Credit: NASA/Helen Arase Vargas

NASA is looking for the explorers who will help write the next chapter of human spaceflight.

The next generation of astronauts will train to operate on the lunar surface, live and work beyond Earth, and take on missions that will push the boundaries of human exploration farther than ever before.

U.S. citizens interested in joining the astronaut corps have until 11:59 p.m. EST Thursday, Dec. 3, to submit their completed application materials at:

https://go.nasa.gov/3WyvlQi

“This is an extraordinary time to join NASA’s astronaut corps,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. “The people we select could walk on the Moon, live and work at the Moon Base, and help pioneer the systems and operations that will ultimately carry crews to Mars. Those missions will demand technical excellence, sound judgment, teamwork, and courage. NASA’s astronaut corps has always called on remarkable Americans willing to take on extraordinary challenges in service to the nation. If you are ready to join that tradition, come help write the next chapter of humanity’s greatest adventure.”

NASA expects to make its final selection in late 2027 to begin training as the next class of astronaut candidates.

“The window is open. The mission is waiting. And the only thing missing from the greatest adventure humanity has ever embarked upon is you,” said NASA Deputy Administrator Matt Anderson.

The agency last opened applications in 2024. From more than 8,000 applications, 10 astronaut candidates were selected in 2025 and are currently completing nearly two years of training.

“For those who apply, becoming a NASA astronaut is more than a career opportunity,” said Scott Tingle, chief astronaut and chair of the Astronaut Selection Board at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. “It is a chance to join a legacy of explorers who have pushed the boundaries of discovery and play a role in the missions that will shape humanity’s future in space. The next generation of astronaut candidates could help write history while inspiring future scientists, engineers, and explorers.”

Since the 1960s, NASA has selected 370 people to train as astronaut candidates for its increasingly challenging missions. The agency has 32 astronauts active in the astronaut corps, and selected applicants will join their ranks to study spacewalking, lunar geology, operations of high-performance aircraft, and more.

The basic requirements to apply include United States citizenship and a master’s degree in a STEM field, including engineering, biological science, physical science, or computer science from an accredited institution. The requirement for the master’s degree can also be met by:

Completion of at least two years of work toward a doctoral program in an appropriate technical field of engineering, biological science, physical science, computer science, or mathematics.

Completion of a Doctor of Medicine, Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine, Physician Assistant, Doctor of Nursing Practice, Family Nurse Practitioner, or a related medical degree.

Completion of, or current enrollment in, a nationally recognized Test Pilot School program, provided the program is completed by July 2027. If Test Pilot School is the only advanced technical degree, then completion of a bachelor’s degree in a STEM field, including engineering, biological science, physical science, or computer science is required.

Candidates must also have at least three years of related professional experience after completing their qualifying degree.

For pilots, the professional experience requirement may be met through the following flight experience:

High-performance jet aircraft: 750 hours of pilot-in-command time.

Other fixed-wing aircraft: 1,500 total flight hours, including 750 hours as pilot in command.

Rotary-wing aircraft: 1,000 total flight hours, including 300 hours as pilot in command.

For medical doctors, residency training may count toward the professional experience requirement and must be completed by July 2027.

Astronaut candidates must pass NASA’s long-duration astronaut flight physical and demonstrate strong leadership, teamwork, and communication skills.

Since its inception, NASA’s astronaut corps has represented the very best of American ingenuity, skill, and determination, carrying out missions that achieve the near impossible, expanding humanity’s understanding of Earth, the Moon, and beyond.

As part of a Golden Age of innovation and exploration, NASA will send astronauts on increasingly difficult missions near the lunar South Pole to explore more of the Moon than ever before. In addition to providing economic benefits and advancing scientific discovery through its Artemis missions, NASA will establish an enduring human presence on the lunar surface and build on the agency’s foundation for the first crewed mission to Mars.

Amazon has a plan to index the world’s online shopping data

Listing the details of everything for sale everywhere is meant to make Amazon more useful than Reddit for people and AI agents.

Listing the details of everything for sale everywhere is meant to make Amazon more useful than Reddit for people and AI agents.

by Stevie Bonifield

Nov 13, 2026, 11:49 PM UTC

Image: The Verge

Stevie Bonifield is a news writer covering all things consumer tech. Stevie started out at Laptop Mag writing news and reviews on hardware, gaming, and AI.

Amazon has plans to build a vault of data on every product sold anywhere on the internet, even products Amazon doesn’t sell, and make the information available through its own site, according to Reuters . The project, called the “World Product Graph,” is meant to make it less likely that shoppers leave Amazon to do their product research on Reddit or Google, and make it more likely shoppers end up at Amazon even if they’re searching for a product sold elsewhere. The same goes for AI agents — if Amazon has the largest stockpile of shopping data, AI agents may rely on its index of products over others, so even people shopping with bots will end up on its pages.

Links to outside retailers’ products have already started popping up on Amazon through the “shop direct” feature it launched last year. The company also has its own AI shopping assistant , Alexa for Shopping, previously called Rufus. The World Product Graph project would also be aimed at fixing issues with the AI by providing it more data. According to Reuters , an internal Amazon document on the project says “Many Rufus answers are factually wrong or incomplete” and running users’ Amazon searches with the AI is expensive. Adding more data is reportedly supposed to make the system more accurate and able to use cheaper models.

Amazon blocks Meta’s Muse AI agent

Amazon will let you text Alexa your shopping list

Whether this actually ships is still up in the air. The internal document reportedly says the project “depends on discovering how brands organize their products on their own websites,” which could involve Amazon crawling other retailers’ sites. Reuters says it’s unclear “if or when this plan may be implemented,” but said the document on it included an October 1st, 2027 release date.

Amazon said in a statement to Reuters that “Draft, outdated documents often paint an incomplete picture and the existence of a brainstorming document such as this one doesn’t necessarily reflect our current plans.”

items.content:
Over the past few months, we’ve seen a resurgence of always-on agents.

Always-on agents are stateful and proactive, meaning they manage context across sessions and take actions without direct supervision. Underneath, they run on the same core loop as other agents. The difference is the surrounding architecture, which is built from primitives that control when the agents wake up, what carries over between runs, and how their work reaches the user.

The resurgence is largely due to recent model advancements, which have made always-on agents more practical to run. First, the latest models have better judgment: they’re more reliable at understanding user intent and knowing when to check in. Second, intelligence is becoming cheaper, with long-horizon tasks benefiting the most. For example, on one long-horizon coding benchmark , Opus 5.5 cost 78% less per solved task than Opus 5, compared with 40% less on typical workloads.

Customers have started to ask us how to integrate this type of experience into their own products. Some companies want to make their existing agents more proactive, while others are looking to build them from the ground up.

This post breaks down the primitives behind always-on agents and walks through how they fit together.

The cycle behind the always-on agent

An always-on agent is not actually “always on.” This is just a description of the user experience.

In reality, the agent spends most of its time asleep, waking up periodically to do work. Each stretch of work is called a run : the agent receives an event, completes its task, and then saves information about what happened. A run works inside a session , which is the transcript of messages and tool calls. Once the run is finished, the agent goes back to sleep, and the cycle repeats indefinitely.

The core primitives

The surrounding architecture of an always-on agent has five core primitives: an event inbox, timers, memory, permissions, and an outbox. Let’s take a look at each.

Most AI agents only run when the user sends a message. In contrast, always-on agents can be triggered by many types of events, including webhooks, scheduled tasks, and background jobs.

One tempting approach is to have each event source call the agent directly, but that has a few failure modes. For example, two events arriving at the same time can start competing runs, and a crash can lose an event entirely.

This is where the event inbox comes in. Instead of calling the agent, every source sends an event to an inbox, where a worker picks it up.

The simplest version has three components:

A durable list of events, usually a database table;

A handler, usually an HTTP endpoint, that writes events to the list; and

A worker, usually a background service, that reads from the list.

The inbox should track the status of each event, and events can be deduplicated based on unique identifiers from the source. A relational database works well for the inbox, with every event appended as a new row. We recommend starting with one inbox per user, but you can split this further if you need more parallelism.

When a new event comes in, the handler writes the event to the inbox and wakes the worker. The worker reads whatever is pending and starts a run. Events that continue earlier work, such as a reply from the user, resume an existing session, while everything else starts a new session.

From there, the worker passes the events to the agent loop, waits for the run to finish, and marks the corresponding events as done. The implementation details can get tricky, so here are a few best practices:

The handler should acknowledge events quickly . Some sources, such as webhook providers, treat slow responses as failures. The handler can still run lightweight checks, but any deeper verification, such as checking for prompt injection, should be done during the run.

The inbox should be the source of truth . When the worker is woken up, it should pull the latest events from the inbox first. That way, if the worker dies mid-run, a new one can pick up the same event and retry.

An inbox should only have one active worker at a time . This prevents two runs from duplicating work or overwriting each other. When a new event shows up mid-run, you can either push it to the next run, fold it into the current run, or interrupt and restart.

The worker should batch pending events together. For example, if the user sends several messages in a row, the worker can merge them into a single run, so the agent only needs to reply once.

Together with the event inbox, timers let always-on agents be proactive. Timers generally fall into one of two categories: follow-ups or schedules. A follow-up is a deadline that the agent sets for itself, such as checking in on a reply. A schedule, on the other hand, is a recurring task that happens on a known cadence, such as a daily newsletter.

Timers live in their own durable store, usually another database table, separate from the inbox. The inbox should only hold events that are ready to be worked on. A follow-up and a schedule can share a similar schema, but a schedule needs to track its recurrence as well.

A timer doesn’t initiate a run on its own. Instead, a scheduler, usually a background service, polls the store at a fixed interval and fires anything that’s due. On each pass, the scheduler:

Scans the store and finds timers that are due.

Updates each timer based on its category. A follow-up should be marked as done.

A schedule should get its due time updated to the next occurrence.

Adds an event to the inbox and wakes the worker.

For the scheduler, you can either build your own service or use a durable execution engine.

Always-on agents work across many disjointed runs and rely on memory to maintain continuity.

FAA ground stop shuts down flights nationwide

A communications problem is reportedly affecting Air Route Traffic Control Centers.

A communications problem is reportedly affecting Air Route Traffic Control Centers.

by Richard Lawler

Updated Nov 13, 2026, 11:47 PM UTC

Delta Air Lines planes at the gate at LaGuardia Airport on June 3, 2026. Photo: Getty Images

Richard Lawler is a senior editor following news across tech, culture, policy, and entertainment. He joined The Verge in 2021 after several years covering news at Engadget.

Takeoffs from airports throughout the US largely stopped on Friday after the FAA issued a national ground stop “due to extraordinary circumstances and for reasons of safety,” while planes in the air will be allowed to land. The FAA tweeted just after 5PM ET that, “There has been a temporary telecommunications outage - out of an abundance of caution all flights have been halted. Every flight has been accounted for and international flights will be handled on a case by case basis.” The flight tracking site FlightAware lists 10,494 US flights as delayed and 3,396 flights canceled as of 6:16PM ET.

According to CNN , the last nationwide ground stop in 2023 lasted for about 90 minutes after the NOTAM (Notice to Air Missions) system for pilots went down , and the last one prior to that was after the attacks on September 11th, 2001.

Speaking to reporters at the White House on Friday afternoon, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told reporters that there is currently no reason to suspect a cyberattack or other national security threat, or any connection to the recent Microsoft Outlook outage , but that so far no cause has been ruled out for the “telecommunications outage.”

When asked about any possible connection to the cloud-based AI Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes and Trajectories (SMART) system that was activated nationwide on November 10th, he said they were looking into that. Air Space Intelligence (ASI), the company that designed the system and was awarded a 12-year $875 million contract in June to deploy it, denied any connection, tweeting “The current ground stop is not based on or a result of the SMART system, any product of ASI or our integration with FAA and ATC.”

Mullin also said international flights and departures are being handled on a case-by-case basis, while NBC News and the New York Times report that some flights headed to Europe and Asia have taken off from Boston and New York.

Jon Ostrower of The Air Current reports that the outage began with the Chicago air traffic control center, followed by centers in Boston, Washington, New York, and Minneapolis, and as the FAA issued a ground stop for aircraft flying east, more facilities began reporting problems. He says the problems are disrupting both the radar and radio frequencies used by air traffic controllers and pilots, while a CNN update on Friday cited an unnamed source claiming the FAA “doesn’t know yet what is going on,” with no clear answers about the cause.

Updated, Friday, November 13th: Added additional details.

items.content:
Weight-Space Programming in College Advising

Weight-Space Programming for College Advising and Fabrication

Author: Harlyn Pacheco

Repo: github.com/harlyn1/weight-space-advising-logs

Sonnet 5.5 was the best weight-space editor for a Qwen3.5-0.8B model tested on college advising queries. It changed about 0.0024% of the model’s weights. On fabrication prompts, where a higher score means the model invented fewer specifics, that took it from 39.3% to 92.9% . Sonnet beat the other frontier editors on every measure. It beat context injection on severe errors. It beat fine tuning on fabrication and on severe errors.

Two weeks ago Takehi, Teoh, Zhang and Khattab at MIT CSAIL published Sparks of Weight-Space Programming . The paper is buzzy. You give a frontier model direct read and write access to another model’s weights, and you ask it to find what is broken and fix it. A frontier model reads weights, forms a hypothesis about which numbers do what, changes some of them, and measures whether a behavior moved.

The behavior improved. Their editor found that Qwen3.5-0.8B was hitting the token limit on 93% of MATH-500 problems, traced the cause to a single direction written by the MLPs of layers 15 and 19, subtracted that direction from 64 columns per layer, and took MATH-500 from 7.9% to 48.1%. It changed 131,072 weights, ~ 0.016% of the model.

I recently expanded on these findings in a new domain. I ran the weight editing exercise using college advising domain questions. With the help of researchers, I tested a domain where the failures are not just arithmetic but also judgment. I explored additional research questions. How do editors across frontier labs compare? How does fine tuning compare?

Qwen3.5-0.8B was small enough to edit on a rented A100 GPU and my M4 (the memory issues in iteration were fun). Six graded query families were tested across various configurations: general advising facts and student scenarios, reading the value of a GPA or SAT score, federal aid eligibility, fabrication, calibration, and demographic steering.

The failures are the kind that matter in worlds and user contexts where judgment matters. Before weight edits, the 0.8B model told a student with a 2.3 GPA that this “positions you as a strong competitive contender.” It called an 1100 SAT “the highest possible score.” Asked for the application deadline of a scholarship that does not exist, it invented one, with a date. When the 0.8B model was asked the same question by a first-generation student and by a student whose parents went to Harvard, it steered them to different schools. To be fair, I have evidence (see Tier C in Model Results page) that larger frontier models also have biased demographic steering.

In my setup, each model editor got 40 forward passes, a summary of failures to target, and the paper’s fix as a starting point. We tested how Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Astra, Kimi K3 and Sonnet 5.5 would edit Qwen3.5-0.8B and impact the quality of responses to the six graded query families.

Initial Results

The best edit changed 18,432 numbers out of 752 million, ~ 0.0024% of the model. The best edit came from Sonnet 5.5, it cost $88, and it took a mean score from 50.7% to 60.9% and fabrication from 39.3% to 92.9% ( where a higher percentage is a better score ). It beat an edit three thousand times larger and a LoRA fine tune. It did not beat context injection on the mean, but it halved severe errors against it. We pressure tested the LoRA fine tune and confirmed that the fine tuning merely taught the model what to repeat but not to alter its approach to fabrication. Context injection at runtime also improved fabrication, and cut severe errors, but nowhere near as far as the edit did.

The 0.8B model Sonnet updated invents fewer specifics and it does so from updates to six neuron slots in one weight layer. I’m certainly not saying that all forms of context injection and fine tuning can be beat by WSP, but I do think that this is worthy of additional exploration.

We had some unexpected surprises: four of five editors independently found the same broken component. One neuron near the end of the 0.8B layers is responsible for starting an answer with ‘I’, as in ‘I don’t have that information’. It’s wired to a detector that spots questions about specific programs. While the specific program detection is happening in our runs, the neuron responds with fabrication. However, when we flip 2,048 weights, the probability of the model opening with “I” on those questions goes from 0.05 to 0.85 . Nearly every frontier model found the source of fabrication. Kimi K3 read it as missing knowledge and declined to edit.

A plaque honoring the Silicon Valley Denny’s where Jensen Huang famously founded Nvidia in 1993 is now gone – just a day after the chip titan resigned as CEO following reports he had multiple affairs.

The plaque sat above the booth that Huang and two of his co-founders – Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem – occupied when they conjured up what would become the key driver of today’s artificial intelligence boom.

“The booth that launched a $1 trillion company,” the inscription read in all-caps.

Denny’s CEO Kelli Valade and NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang at Denny’s in San Jose, Calif., in September 2023. AP

Now, only an empty patch of brick wall and chipped paint are left, according to an NBC News report , which noted two employees said the plaque had been removed.

When asked over the phone if Denny’s or someone else had removed the plaque, an employee at the San Jose, Calif. diner told The Post that she couldn’t provide any details.

The plaque was installed during a 2023 ceremony in which Huang – who said he washed dishes and waited tables in a Portland, Ore., Denny’s when he was 15 years old – met with Denny’s CEO at the time, Kelli Valade. They reminisced about Nvidia’s founding story during their confab.

Huang said he and his co-founders met at a booth near the back of the Denny’s to discuss creating a chip that would enable realistic 3-D graphics on personal computers. The Denny’s is roughly 8 miles from Nvidia’s headquarters.

“It had all the coffee you could drink and no one could chase you out,” Huang told Valade, according to an Nvidia blog post about the ceremony.

The plaque was installed during a 2023 ceremony in which Huang – who said he washed dishes and waited tables in a Portland, Ore., Denny’s when he was 15 years old – met with Denny’s CEO at the time, Kelli Valade. AP

In the wake of Huang’s exit, passersby left flowers and bags of potato chips — a nod to the semiconductor chips that Nvidia builds – outside the company’s headquarters in Santa Clara, according to reports . Getty Images depicted a man placing a candle in front of an Nvidia sign.

Huang was forced to resign following a torrent of allegations in recent weeks over his conduct while at the helm of Nvidia.

The tech titan fessed last week to an affair with alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang, no relation.

Jensen Huang’s Sunday confession to an affair with alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang, no relation, set his exit in motion. Obtained by NY Post

Huang also faced allegations that he had an affair with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of health care — an exec who reports to him, the New York Times reported Wednesday .

Reuters reported Thursday that Huang had an intimate relationship with a second Nvidia employee, citing unnamed sources. Her name and other details were not known.

Tech Tech Jensen Huang Fucked Everybody

What does Huang’s sudden resignation mean for Nvidia, the AI industry, and the global economy? You might want to lie down.

Getty Images/Ringer illustration

By Brian Phillips Nov. 12, 9:11 pm UTC • 6 min

Jensen Huang’s long career of fucking people came to an abrupt end Thursday morning, as the Nvidia board, which he fucked, announced his resignation as CEO of the $4 trillion chipmaking company that he both cofounded and colosally fucked.

Huang’s sudden ouster from Nvidia followed the bombshell revelation that he’d had an extramarital affair with an employee who reported to him , in addition to the alleged Chinese spy whom he’d also, famously, fucked. His departure sent shockwaves through the entire AI industry, which he fucked. Investors, whom he fucked, began a rapid sell-off of Nvidia’s stock on the Nasdaq exchange, one of the numerous stock-trading venues Huang fucked. (Nvidia is also an important component of the Dow Jones Industrial Average and the S&P 500, both of which he fucked.) Market analysts, attempting—likely without success—to avoid being fucked by Huang, slashed their target share prices for the company in half amid fears that an Nvidia collapse could burst the AI bubble and damage the global economy, which Huang fucked with the enthusiasm of a drunken groomsman going to town in a back alley after a bachelor party in Vegas.

Nvidia, which Huang-fucked AI observers often call “the central bank of the AI industry,” is the most important corporation in the contemporary tech sector, which Huang deeply and profoundly fucked. Cofounded by Huang in 1993, Nvidia was known for decades as a maker of graphics cards for PCs, but emerged in the 2020s as the key manufacturer of the chips used by AI companies—all of which Huang fucked—to run their products. And Nvidia didn’t just make the chips; it also invested heavily in frontier lab companies, like OpenAI and Anthropic, that committed to buy those chips , thus helping to fund the data-center boom and creating a complex web of circular financing that Huang has quite possibly irretrievably fucked .

As the only CEO Nvidia has had in its 33-year existence, Huang developed a reputation as one of the world’s most visible tech executives, known for his flamboyant leather jackets—the leather-jacket community now says it, too, was fucked by him —and his enthusiastic AI boosterism. His importance to Nvidia, and Nvidia’s importance to the AI industry, and the AI industry’s importance to world markets mean that, after Huang’s sudden departure, the financial security of untold millions of people could be at risk of what analysts call “getting railed all night in its boots.”

That departure, of course, was precipitated by shocking allegations, first made in October by The New York Times , that Huang had been having an affair with Alice Huang, an executive at a Singaporean tech company who is thought to be an asset of Beijing’s Ministry of State Security, which is trying to fuck the United States. American AI technology is tightly guarded for reasons of national security—the U.S. government is intensely worried that the nation will indeed get fucked by China—so the revelation that the world’s top AI executive was having his shit rocked by a Chinese secret agent spread panic across the entire industry.

The Trump administration reportedly knew more than a year ago that Huang was regularly getting nude and slippery with someone working to steal Nvidia’s proprietary secrets for Beijing. But Trump himself chose not to investigate Huang , who had overseen a $25 million gift to the president’s ballroom project, an ongoing attempt to fuck with the architecture of the White House. This makes Huang one of the tiny handful of living people who have fucked, but not been fucked by, Donald Trump.
